This Miscellaneous First Appeal having been heard through Physical Hearing/Video Conferencing, reserved for Judgment on 09.03.2023, coming on for pronouncement this day, the Court delivered the following:
JUDGMENT

The present appeal is filed by the claimant under Section 173 (1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988,
seeking enhancement of the compensation awarded by the learned Senior Civil Judge and J.M.F.C.,
and Addl.Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, Sira, (hereinafter for brevity referred to as 'the Tribunal'), in its judgment and award dated 15.12.2018, in M.V.C.No.433/2017.
2.

The summary of the case of the present appellant as claimant before the Tribunal was that, on the date 23.06.2016, at about 3.00 p.m., while he was proceeding on his motorcycle bearing registration No.KA-06-EJ-77 along with pillion rider by name Syed Shabuddin from Sira towards Changavara to go to Dharmapura, near Sakkara village cross, a bus bearing registration No.KA-06-D-0558, being driven by its driver in a rash and negligent manner, coming from opposite direction, dashed to his motorcycle, as a result of the said road traffic accident, both of them fell down from the motorcycle and he sustained bodily injuries.
Immediately, he was shifted to Government Hospital, Sira and from there to Hemavathi Orthopedic and Trauma Centre, Tumakuru.

entities.text: Hemavathi Orthopedic and Trauma Centre, Tumakuru
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text:
After taking further treatment,
he was shifted to Vikram Hospital at Bengaluru, wherein, he was admitted as an inpatient.
The claimant has also stated that he has spent `10 lakhs towards medicines and other incidental expenses.
He further stated that, at the time of accident, he was aged 43 years and working as a businessman, electrician and agriculturist and was earning a sum of `40,000/- per month.
All his family members were entirely depending upon his income.
Due to the injuries suffered by him, he is suffering from permanent physical disability to the whole body, as such, he cannot do any work as earlier and lost his earning capacity.
Holding the respondent Nos.1 and 2, who are owner and insurer of the offending vehicle respectively, the claimant has claimed in total a compensation of `65 lakhs from them.
3. After service of notice, the respondent No.1 remained absent, as such, he was placed ex parte.

The respondent No.2, which is the Insurance Company, appearing through its counsel, filed its statement of objections denying the averments made in the claim petition and contended that by colluding with jurisdictional police, the claimant got registered a false case.
It contended that the accident occurred due to the fault of the claimant's motorcycle and not due to the alleged negligent act on the part of driver of the alleged offending vehicle.
It also contended that the driver of the bus did not have valid and effective driving licence.
It denied the income and alleged disability of the claimant.
With this, it prayed to dismiss the claim petition.
Before the Tribunal, the claimant got himself examined as PW-1 and also examined one Dr.Chethan Nagaraj as PW-2 and got marked documents from Exs.P-1 to P-27.

On behalf of the respondents,

neither any witness was examined nor any documents were produced.

4. After analysing the evidence and the materials placed before it, the Tribunal has awarded the compensation under the following heads with the sum shown against them:

The Tribunal awarded compensation of a sum of `21,00,040/- with interest at `6% per annum thereupon from the date of petition till the date of realisation, holding the owner and Insurer jointly and severally liable to pay the said compensation and directed the Insurer to deposit the award amount.
It is against the said judgment and award passed by the Tribunal, the claimant has filed this appeal seeking enhancement of compensation.
6. The respondent No.2 herein (insurer) is represented by its counsel.

Notice to respondent No.1 is dispensed with vide Court order dated 22.09.2022.
7.
Records from the Tribunal pertaining to the matter were called for and the same are placed before the Court.
8. Though this appeal is posted for admission, with the consent from both parties, the matter was taken up for arguments on main on merits.
9. Heard the arguments of learned counsel for the appellant and learned counsel for respondent No.2-Insurance Company.

Perused the materials placed before this Mohammed Ibrahim vs Shivashankar on 20 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/175861295/
3 Court, including memorandum of appeal, impugned judgment and records of the Tribunal.
10.

The present appeal being the claimant's appeal and respondent No.2 (insurer)
having not preferred either cross- objection or a counter appeal, the question of occurrence of accident on the date, time and place as alleged by the claimant and also the alleged rash and negligent driving on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle is not in dispute.

Further, the claimant got himself examined as PW-1, who in his evidence has reiterated the contentions taken up by him in his claim petition regarding the manner of occurrence of accident and involvement of the vehicles in question.

His evidence is further corroborated through Exs.P-1 to P-11, P-20, P-21, P-22 to P-26 and P-27, which inter alia includes copies of FIR, complaint, wound certificate, discharge summary, two discharge cards, twentysix X-ray films, four CT Scans, five case sheets and charge sheet.

11. Thus, the occurrence of the road traffic accident and the present appellant sustained injuries in the said road traffic accident and also of the fact that the said road traffic accident occurred at the rash and negligent driving by the driver of the bus bearing registration No.KA-06-D-0558, stands established.

Therefore, the question of occurrence of accident and the alleged liability of the respondent-Insurance Company to pay compensation to the injured claimant for the injuries sustained by him in the road traffic accident need not be re-analysed again.
As such, the only question that remains to be considered is about the quantification of the compensation, which according to the claimant/appellant is inadequate.
12. The learned counsel for the appellant (claimant) in his argument submitted that the income of the injured was taken by the Tribunal at `12,000/- per month, which is on the lower side.
Considering the evidence of the claimant, his income ought to have been taken at `22,000/- per month.
He also submits that the Tribunal has not applied the future prospects while computing the compensation.
He further submitted that the disability should have been taken by the Tribunal at 100% since the same is the functional disability which has disabled the claimant from pursuing his avocation.

He also submitted that the Tribunal though titled the compensation as medical,
conveyance, nutrition and attendant charges, it has considered only the medical expenses for reimbursement, but, towards nutrition and attendant charges, it has not been considered.
He also submitted that future medical expenses for removal of implants has not been awarded by the Tribunal.
With this, he prayed for allowing the appeal as prayed.

13. Per contra, learned counsel for respondent No.2- Insurance Company in his brief argument submitted that the quantification of compensation is in accordance with law and the Tribunal has considered the entire evidence led before it while calculating the compensation, as such, the same does not warrant any interference at the hands of this Court.

He further submitted that the alleged disability since would not come in the way of avocation of the claimant resulting in his total disablement, the Tribunal has rightly confined the percentage of disability only to 44% of the whole Mohammed Ibrahim vs Shivashankar on 20 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/175861295/
4
body , as such, the same also does not warrant any interference at the hands of this Court.

14. The claimant as PW-1 in his examination-in-chief has stated that in the road traffic accident,
which is the subject matter of the claim petition, he sustained multiple grievous injuries.
His right leg was crushed and several of the nerves got cut and the muscles were compressed.

After diagnosis,
the doctor has stated that the claimant has sustained multiple fractures.
However, the witness could not able to mention the exact nature of the injuries in medical terms.

On the other hand, PW-2 Dr.Chethan Nagaraj, who is said to be a Consultant Orthopedic Surgeon at Vikram Hospital, Bengaluru, has stated that he has examined the claimant on 23.06.2016 and found the following injuries :
(1) Compound fracture of right femur with neurovascular injury (2) Compound fracture (Grade II) right tibia and fibula (3) Patellar dislocation of right knee (4)
Fractures of right distal radius - intra articular (5) Fracture of nasal bones
The witness has opined that all these injuries were grievous in nature.
The claimant has produced the copy of wound certificate shown to have been issued by the Medical Officer, Taluk General Hospital, Sira, at Ex.P-3.

He has also produced discharge summary shown to have been issued by Vikram Hospital (Bengaluru) Pvt. Ltd., at Ex.P-4, which shows that the claimant was treated as an inpatient in their hospital from 23.06.2016 to 02.07.2016.

It has diagnosed the injuries as below :
(1) Grade III C Compound fracture right femur M/3 with neurovascular injury (2)
Grade II compound fracture BB right leg M/3-D/3 (3) Patellar ligament avulsion (4)
Right distal, radius intra articular fracture (5) Vascular trauma femoral artery injury with thrombosis.
Thus, the medical documents, coupled with the evidence of the doctor as PW-2 shows that the claimant sustained five grievous injuries and was treated as an inpatient in the hospital.
Thus, he must have suffered greater pain due to the injuries suffered by him in the road traffic accident.
The Tribunal without discussing about the nature of the injures, has awarded a compensation of `50,000/- towards `pain and suffering'.

However, considering the nature of the injuries suffered by the claimant, I am of the view that the said quantum of compensation is slightly on the lower side, as such, it requires to be enhanced by a sum of `20,000/-, thus, making it to a total sum of `70,000/-.

Thus, the claimant is entitled to an enhanced compensation of a sum of `20,000/- towards `pain and suffering', making it to a total sum of `70,000/-.
15.
The claimant has stated that he was a businessman, doing electrical and hardware business and was earning a sum of `2,50,000/- per annum.
He also stated that from agriculture, he was earning an income of `2,50,000/- per annum.

In support of his contention, he has produced four years Income-tax returns at Ex.P-14, copy of the GST Registration Certificate for his business at Ex.P-15 and also a copy of the order of the Lease to show that he had taken a premises on lease from Sira Town Municipality at Ex.P-16.
He had produced RTC extract of a land at Exs.P-17 and P-18.
The Income-tax returns at Ex.P-14 is for the Assessment Year 2013-14, 2014-15, 2015-16 and 2017-18.

sentences.text: The road traffic accident since has taken place in June 2016, the immediate preceding Financial Year, for which, Assessment Year is 2016-17, has not been produced by the claimant for the reasons best known to him.
However, the Income-tax returns for the Assessment Year 2015-16 shows that he has declared his gross total income at `2,50,420/-.
Except RTC, no other documents to show the agricultural produce or agricultural income has been produced by him.
The Tribunal has taken his monthly income at `12,000/- per month.
Since his declared income for the Assessment Year 2015-16 itself is `2,50,420/-, his monthly income would come to `20,868/-, rounded off to `21,000/-.
As such, the Tribunal should have taken his monthly income at `21,000/- per month.
For the injuries suffered by him, as observed above, the Tribunal has opined that he must have required and taken rest for a period of six months.
However, the medical documents produced by him would go to show that he was treated at four different dates as inpatient in the hospital, which in total was coming to thirtytwo days.
Still, since the Tribunal has considered his laid up period as six months, the loss of income for the said six months laid up period is `21,000/-x6=`1,26,000/-.
Since the Tribunal has awarded a sum of `72,000/-, the claimant is entitled for a differential amount of `54,000/- under the said head.
16 . The claimant has also contended that due to the accident and the injuries suffered by him, he is suffering with total disability, as such, he could not do any business and any activity.
Dr.Chethan Nagaraj (PW-2 who examined him, has assessed the physical disability at 88% of lower limb and around 44% to the whole body.
The Tribunal has taken the said 44% as the percentage of disability to assess the quantum of compensation towards future loss of income of the claimant.

Learned counsel for the appellant in his argument vehemently submitted that since the claimant as PW-1 has clearly stated that he has become totally disabled and admittedly he has undergone surgery for about five times, the functional disability should have been taken at 100%.

The said argument of learned counsel for the appellant is not acceptable for the reason that the claimant who claims to have owning an immovable property, running business by getting a lease of shop premise, has produced the GST Registration Certificate also.

Had he not running the business and stopped it and had he not continuing the agricultural activities through workman, he would have produced the documents of closure of his business, may be declaration to the taxation authorities and entries in the RTC and land records show that land is not being cultivated.

On the contrary, the claimant himself as at Ex.P-14 produced his Income-tax returns for the year 2017-18,
which is for the Financial Year 2016-17, wherein his income is shown at `1,01,756/-.
17.

Thus, even after the road traffic accident and even during the laid up period also, for which his total loss of income was compensated as above as loss of income during laid up period, he had in fact some income though in a reduced amount.

Thus, the disability has not stopped his business,
however, immediately after the accident, for that particular year, he had a lower income compared to two years prior to the accident.

Therefore, the percentage of disability cannot be considered as 100% and according to the evidence of PW-2, the doctor, the percentage of disability is at 44% to the whole body, which also has been accepted by the Tribunal without any variation and the same cannot be found fault with.

sentences.text: According to the judgment of the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of National Insurance Company Limited Vs. Pranay Sethi and Others reported in (2017) 16 SCC 680, for the future prospects, the income of the claimant has to be taken into consideration.

entities.text: National Insurance Company Limited Vs. Pranay Sethi and Others reported in (2017) 16 SCC 680
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Undisputedly, the age of the claimant was 43 years as at the time of the accident as could be seen in the hospital records.
As such, the multiplier applicable is `14' to his age.
The claimant was a self- employed person, as such, the rate of future prospects would be 25% of his income.
Thus, his monthly income for the purpose of calculation of loss of future income would be `21,000/-+`5,250/- (25% of `21,000/-) = `26,250/-.

Thus, the compensation towards future loss of income would be `26,250/-x12x14x44/100 =
`19,40,400/-.
Since the Tribunal has awarded a sum of `8,87,040/-, the claimant is entitled for a differential amount of `10,53,360/- as enhancement towards loss of future income.

19. The Tribunal though has confined the medical expenses amount at `10,40,947/- and rounded it off to `10,41,000/- after considering 101 medical bills at Ex.P-13 and 44 medical prescriptions at Ex.P-12, however, it also covers the other heads of compensation like nutrition, attendant charges and conveyance also within the said amount.

Since `10,41,000/- is only with respect to the medical expenses incurred by the claimant and since the claimant was inpatient in the hospital for thirtytwo days in total, I am of the view that he is entitled at the rate of `800/- per day towards `nutrition,
attendant charges and conveyance'.
Thus, it comes to `25,600/-, for which, the claimant is entitled to.

Thus, towards `medical expenses, nutrition, attendant charges and conveyance', in total the claimant is entitled for a compensation of a sum of `10,66,600/-
20.

The quantification towards `loss of future life and amenities' the Tribunal has awarded a sum of `50,000/- and the same being a reasonable amount in the facts and circumstances of the case, it does not warrant any modification.
21. Barring the above, the claimant/appellant is not entitled for compensation under any other heads or for enhancement of compensation under any other heads.

Thus, in total the appellant is entitled for the modified compensation as below :

It is for this enhancement amount only, the present appeal deserves to be allowed.

22. Accordingly, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
[i] The appeal filed by the claimant stands allowed in part;

[ii] The impugned judgment and award passed by the learned Senior Civil Judge and J.M.F.C., and Addl.Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, Sira dated 15.12.2018, in M.V.C.No.433/2017, is hereby modified to the extent that the compensation awarded at `21,00,040/- is enhanced by a sum of `11,52,960/-(Rupees Eleven Lakhs Fiftytwo thousand Nine hundred and Sixty only) thus fixing the total compensation at `32,53,000/- (Rupees Thirtytwo lakhs Fiftythree thousand only).

[iii] The rest of the order of the Tribunal with respect to fixing the liability upon the respondents and directing the respondent No.2 -Insurance Company to deposit the awarded amount,
awarding the interest, its rate, terms regarding release of the amount awarded shall remain unaltered.
[iv] However, as per the order dated 27.10.2022, the appellant/claimant is not entitled for interest for the delayed period of 271 days in filing the present appeal.
Draw the modified award accordingly.
Registry to transmit a copy of this judgment to the concerned Tribunal along with its records without delay.
